summary: Deep design research: flows, journeys, UI/UX references for all 4 Halal Goes apps + palette/icon/map directions, anchored on HungerStation-but-cleaner

primary_references.name: Revyl Atlas — DoorDash Screen Map
primary_references.why: The single most useful reference found: an exhaustive, structured map of 98 real DoorDash iOS screens, 112 transitions, 37 named user paths and a 651-element UI inventory, organized exactly by the flow categories this task needs (home/discovery, store/menu, cart/checkout, order tracking, account, reviews, help). Use it as a checklist of screens/states our customer app must not forget (e.g. 'Store Info Detail Sheet', 'Add Tip Sheet' post-checkout, 'Profile Badges modal', 'Disable Save Login Info confirmation').
key_screens: Checkout: payment + tip + Place order (21 elements)
Order Tracking: Shopping in progress / Dasher Arriving / Complete

primary_references.name: Revyl Atlas — Uber (Eats) Screen Map
primary_references.why: Same structured-atlas approach applied to Uber, including the Eats vertical nested inside the ride-hailing app. Useful for the 'Home tab → checkout in 7 screens' flow shape and for cross-vertical patterns (grocery/alcohol/retail categories reusing the same restaurant-card and PDP shell) that HungerStation-style apps also use for non-restaurant verticals.

primary_references.name: Mobbin — Food Delivery App category
primary_references.why: The canonical screen-by-screen library for this exact brief; direct URLs to individual talabat/Careem/Uber Eats/Grubhub/Grab/Swiggy flows were surfaced via search even though the category index itself 403'd to the fetch tool (it requires a logged-in session — open directly in a browser to browse further).

primary_references.name: talabat iOS — Delivery Tracking Map
primary_references.why: Nearest regional competitor to HungerStation (same Delivery Hero family, same MENA audience) with a live tracking map screen showing progress, ETA and an in-app driver-chat entry point — the pattern to match/clean up for our own tracking screen.

primary_references.name: talabat iOS — Login Options
primary_references.why: Reference for the onboarding/auth screen shape (phone-first with social fallbacks — Google/Facebook/Apple/email) directly comparable to our OTP-first onboarding requirement.

primary_references.name: talabat iOS — Giving Feedback Flow
primary_references.why: Post-order rating/review flow reference: rate, add detail, confirmation — a minimal-friction shape worth mirroring for our ratings/reviews flow.

primary_references.name: Mapbox Showcase — Wolt
primary_references.why: Direct precedent for the client's Mapbox subscription: Wolt uses Mapbox Matrix API (traffic-aware ETA across bike/car/motorcycle/walking couriers, validated with live switchback experiments) for routing/ETA and Static Maps API for lightweight order-tracking map images on web. Confirms Matrix+Static (not just the interactive SDK) is a legitimate architecture for our live-tracking screen, and that ETA accuracy — not map prettiness — is what Wolt optimized first.

primary_references.name: Mapbox — Standard Style customization / Dark & Light basemaps
primary_references.why: Mapbox Standard's Lookup Tables (LUTs) and the Standard Style Theme Editor let us retheme roads, water, buildings and emissive glow per light/dark mode without hand-authoring a full style — the practical route to a theme-matched tracking map for both HG themes.

primary_references.name: Baymard Institute — 'Add Past Purchases to Cart from Homepage'
primary_references.why: Primary UX research (not a competitor screenshot) establishing that reorder/'Order Again' surfaces belong on the homepage in the first viewport, not buried in order history — users are equally likely to look for a reorder in either place, and its absence reads as a broken convention.

primary_references.name: Luis Fernandez — Uber Eats, DoorDash and Glovo Checkout Process Analysis
primary_references.why: Direct comparative teardown of three checkout flows (6 steps / 4 steps / 5 steps respectively) with named strengths and weaknesses per app — the best sourced material found for calibrating our own checkout step count and for concrete pitfalls (vague allergy/condiment toggles, missing confirmation screens, tipping-screen cultural sensitivity, service-fee-hidden-in-tax pattern).

primary_references.name: Blake Crosley — Zomato: Personality-Driven Food UX
primary_references.why: Best-sourced material on dietary/trust badges as a first-class visual system (green circle veg / dark-green 'pure veg' badge, distinct from generic ratings) and on turning the live-tracking wait into an emotionally engaged moment — directly relevant to how we badge halal state and design the tracking screen without leaning on red/green misuse.

primary_references.name: Safe Plate Alliance — DoorDash/Uber Eats allergy-safety audit
primary_references.why: Independent audit finding 80% of restaurants on the two largest US apps expose only a generic free-text box for allergen/dietary communication — the cautionary baseline our halal-badge system must beat structurally (a first-class per-item/per-restaurant field, not a comment box).

primary_references.name: Uber — Allergy-Friendly Restaurant Program FAQ
primary_references.why: Uber Eats' actual shipped pattern for a certified-restaurant badge plus a 'DIETARY TYPE' filter (vegetarian/vegan/gluten-free/allergy-friendly) and saved user allergen preferences — structurally the closest existing shipped analogue to a halal-certified filter/badge, including the orange-banner surfacing of a diner's allergy note back to the order screen.

steps: Splash → phone-number entry (country code default CA) — talabat pattern layers social login (Google/Facebook/Apple) below the primary phone field; HG should keep phone/OTP as the sole primary path per O-03 blocker, no social fallback needed for MVP
OTP code entry with auto-read/paste, resend timer, and an explicit 'change number' escape hatch
First-run name + optional email capture (deferred, not blocking access to browse)
Location permission prompt — framed with a plain-language reason (Deliveroo's redesign critique flagged forcing this with no 'not now' option as a top usability complaint; give an explicit skip)
Address confirmation/pin-drop before landing on home
flows.reference: https://mobbin.com/explore/screens/ac4ab7ef-bd7b-42f7-b435-5718353de1a5 (talabat login options); Deliveroo location-permission critique via netguru.com/blog/deliveroo-ux-redesign-case-study
flows.notes: Do not gate home-screen browsing on notification/location permission grants — ask, but let denial degrade gracefully (manual address entry, no push). Pair OTP with a visible halal-mission one-liner on the splash/first-run screen so the app's premise is stated before any menu is seen.

steps: Address bar pinned top (tap to switch saved address) — HungerStation/talabat convention
Search bar entry point (not full search screen) directly below address
Category tile row (illustrated icons) — cuisines plus a distinct 'Halal Certified' filter tile treated as a first-class category, not buried in filters
Promo/banner carousel (HungerStation uses magenta/maroon for these — HG should use the brand gold + tint accents, never solid green here since green is halal-reserved)
'Order Again' reorder rail in the first viewport — Baymard finding: users expect this at home, not only in order history

Restaurant card list/grid: hero photo, name, star rating + review count, delivery-time (shield icon per HungerStation), distance, 'Free delivery' tag, halal badge placed adjacent to the name (top-left corner of the card image, consistent slot across all cards)
flows.reference: https://revyl.com/atlas/doordash/ (Home: food delivery feed, 22 elements); Baymard https://baymard.com/blog/grocery-food-delivery-orders
flows.notes: Missing-halal-field = no badge (invariant #8): the card layout must reserve the badge slot but render nothing rather than a placeholder/greyed icon when the field is null, so absence doesn't visually read as 'checked and failed'.

steps: Search results as typeahead (restaurant + dish level) per DoorDash's 'Search (with typeahead results)' screen

Filter bottom sheet: cuisine, price, rating, delivery time, 'Halal Certified' toggle pinned near the top of the sheet (not alphabetized into obscurity) — mirrors Uber Eats' 'DIETARY TYPE' section pattern but as a trust filter, not a dietary-restriction checkbox
Sort bottom sheet: relevance / rating / delivery time / distance
Applied-filter chips row above results, each removable individually
flows.notes: Because halal is the platform's single load-bearing claim, do not treat it as one checkbox among many dietary tags — give it dedicated visual weight in the filter sheet (its own row/section, not alphabetically interleaved with 'Vegan').

steps: Header: hero photo/banner, name, rating+count, cuisine tags, distance/ETA

Halal certification panel directly below header — not a small icon but a tappable block showing certifying body, expiry, and the seven-check instrument summary; this is the trust centerpiece per the project brief, deserving more real estate than a badge alone
Info row: hours, 'Free delivery' / fee, minimum order
Menu categories as sticky horizontal tabs or vertical anchor-linked sections
Item rows: photo thumbnail, name, price, short description, '+' add button
flows.notes: Never render an optimistic badge while certification data loads — show a skeleton/loading state for the halal panel specifically, distinct from the generic content skeleton, so users never see a flash of 'unverified' or 'green' before data resolves.

steps: Bottom sheet slides up on item tap: large photo, name, price, description
Modifier groups: required single-select (radio) vs optional multi-select (checkbox), each group labeled 'Required' or 'Select up to N'
Quantity stepper bottom-left, price-updating CTA button bottom-right/full-width ('Add to cart · $12.50')
Special-instructions free-text field below modifiers
flows.reference: https://mobbin.com/glossary/bottom-sheet; DoorDash 'Menu item customizer' via https://revyl.com/atlas/doordash/
flows.notes: Pitfall flagged in the Uber Eats/DoorDash/Glovo teardown: DoorDash's condiment toggle is 'too vague for allergy-critical users' — since HG's modifier sheet is where cross-contamination/ingredient questions surface, keep instructions field visible (not collapsed) rather than optional-and-hidden.

steps: Restaurant header pinned, item list with quantity steppers inline
Upsell rail ('Complete your order' / 'In Case You Missed It') below items — optional, must not block checkout CTA
Subtotal → fees → tax breakdown expandable, not collapsed-by-default hiding fees (flagged as a trust-eroding pattern in the checkout teardown)
Sticky bottom CTA 'Go to checkout · $X.XX'
flows.reference: https://luiselias.com/uber-eats-doordash-and-glovo-checkout-process-analysis/ ('hiding service fees with taxes aids acceptance' — flagged as a pattern to avoid, not emulate)
flows.notes: Per invariant #1 (server prices every order), the cart must treat all displayed prices as server-returned, not client-computed from cached item prices — re-fetch/re-price on cart open.

steps: Step 1 — Address + delivery time: confirm/edit saved address, choose ASAP vs scheduled
Step 2 — Cart review with delivery instructions field
Step 3 — Tip selection: percentage chips + custom amount, no amount pre-selected/defaulted high
Step 4 — Payment method select + place-order CTA with a visible order summary, not a silent submit
flows.notes: PITFALL: DoorDash's tip UI has been publicly criticized as a dark pattern — tip pre-selected at 25% and users 'nudged' post-order to raise it. HG should default tip UNSELECTED (or to 0/no-tip highlighted equally among options), never pre-checked at a high percentage. Also from the teardown: Glovo's separate payment step risks data loss on connection failure — keep payment selection in the same screen/state as place-order, not a separate network round-trip screen.

steps: Full-bleed map with route line: restaurant pin → rider pin (live) → customer pin
Status stepper overlay: Placed → Accepted → Preparing → Picked up → Arriving → Delivered, each tied to the order's deadline_at
Rider card: photo, name, vehicle, in-app chat/call CTA
ETA countdown prominent, ETA source is traffic-aware routing (Matrix-API-style), not a static estimate
flows.reference: https://www.mapbox.com/showcase/wolt (Matrix API for traffic-aware ETA + Static Maps API for lightweight tracking images); https://mobbin.com/explore/screens/9cf34fd0-bc79-4de1-9c9f-871eccf4f884 (talabat tracking map); https://blakecrosley.com/guides/design/zomato (turning wait into an engaged moment via humanized rider profile)
flows.notes: Recommend Mapbox Matrix API for ETA computation (validated by Wolt's own switchback experiments at scale) plus Mapbox Standard Style with Lookup-Table theming (docs: mapbox.com/maps/dark, mapbox.com/maps/light) for a route/pin style matched to HG's gold light theme and a genuinely dark dark-theme map — not just an inverted default style.

steps: List of past orders newest-first: restaurant name/photo, date, item summary, total, status chip
Tap into an order for a receipt-style detail view
'Reorder' primary CTA on each row, re-adding items to a fresh cart (re-priced server-side, not restoring the old price)
Empty state (no orders yet): illustration + 'Browse restaurants' CTA, not a bare blank list
flows.notes: Reorder must re-price through the server pricing engine — never replay a cached total, since menu/price changes and item availability may have changed since the original order.

steps: Post-delivery prompt: star rating for restaurant + separate star rating for rider
Optional tags/quick-reasons (e.g. 'Great food', 'Fast delivery') to reduce free-text friction
Optional free-text comment + photo attach
Confirmation screen, dismissible
flows.reference: https://mobbin.com/explore/flows/f84e443e-3e17-43bd-af87-05d409989f14 (talabat feedback flow); DoorDash 'Rate Order: Items, Preferred Shopper' via https://revyl.com/atlas/doordash/
flows.notes: Keep restaurant-food rating and rider-delivery rating visually separate — conflating them (one star for the whole order) is a common competitor weakness since a late rider unfairly tanks restaurant ratings.

steps: Profile hub: avatar, name, phone (masked), edit-info entry
Saved addresses list with labels (Home/Work/Other), map-pin edit, default-address toggle
Wallet: balance, payment methods list, add-card flow, transaction history
Notification preferences: order updates vs promotional, separately toggleable
Notifications feed: order-status pushes, promo pushes, chronological with read/unread state
flows.reference: https://revyl.com/atlas/doordash/ (Account hub, Addresses & Address Details/Edit, Payment Methods, Notifications preferences)
flows.notes: Every list here (addresses, payment methods, notifications, order history) needs an explicit empty state per AGENTS.md 'every screen implements empty, loading and error' — this is a repo-level hard requirement, not just good practice.

ui_patterns.pattern: Halal badge as a dedicated slot, never optimistic
ui_patterns.detail: Reserve a fixed badge position on restaurant cards and the restaurant-page header; render literally nothing when the halal field is null/loading rather than a grey/placeholder icon, per invariant #8. Loading state for the certification panel must be visually distinct from generic skeletons so a 'not yet loaded' state can never be mistaken for 'checked, no badge'.
ui_patterns.seen_in: Uber Eats allergy-friendly badge + DIETARY TYPE filter (help.uber.com); Zomato veg/pure-veg badge system (blakecrosley.com/guides/design/zomato)

ui_patterns.pattern: Trust badge gets a panel, not just an icon
ui_patterns.detail: On the restaurant page, halal certification deserves a tappable block (certifying body, expiry, link to the seven-check detail) rather than a small corner icon — icons are for the list/card view; the page-level moment is where trust is actually established.
ui_patterns.seen_in: Design guidance from erikfiala.com/blog/psychology-trust-seals-badges-ui-design and gapsystudio.com/blog/ux-trust-design — position trust indicators near decision points, not scattered

ui_patterns.pattern: Cool-slate expired state, never red
ui_patterns.detail: Directly maps to a real shipped precedent: apps universally use red/orange for 'allergy warning' banners (Uber Eats' orange cross-contamination banner). HG must deliberately diverge — an expired/unverifiable halal certificate should read as neutral slate/grey, visually distinct from any warning-red used elsewhere in the app for unrelated errors, so users never pattern-match 'red = don't eat this' onto a halal ambiguity.
ui_patterns.seen_in: help.uber.com allergy banner (orange) as the pattern to avoid mimicking for halal state

ui_patterns.pattern: Reorder rail on the homepage, not just in history
ui_patterns.detail: Show a horizontal 'Order Again' carousel with photo thumbnails and one-tap re-add directly on the home feed, in the first viewport — validated UX research finding, not just a competitor screenshot.

ui_patterns.pattern: Shield icon for delivery time
ui_patterns.detail: HungerStation-family apps (talabat) use a small shield glyph next to the delivery-time estimate on restaurant cards, giving ETA a 'guaranteed/protected' visual association distinct from the star-rating glyph — a cheap, reusable bit of iconographic consistency worth adopting for our 'nice consistent icons' requirement.
ui_patterns.seen_in: Client-observed HungerStation videos (per task brief); talabat card conventions

ui_patterns.pattern: Fee breakdown expanded by default at checkout
ui_patterns.detail: Avoid the flagged anti-pattern of folding service fees into 'tax' or collapsing the breakdown to ease sticker shock — show subtotal / delivery fee / service fee / tax as separate visible lines.
ui_patterns.seen_in: Checkout teardown flagging 'hiding service fees with taxes aids acceptance' as a manipulative pattern (luiselias.com)

ui_patterns.pattern: Tip selector with no high default
ui_patterns.detail: Percentage chips (e.g. 10/15/20%) plus custom amount, with none pre-selected, or 'No tip' given equal visual weight — direct response to a publicly criticized dark pattern.

ui_patterns.pattern: Certified-restaurant filter as its own section
ui_patterns.detail: In the filter bottom sheet, give the trust/certification toggle its own row at the top rather than alphabetizing it among generic dietary tags (vegan, gluten-free) — signals platform-level guarantee vs. per-user preference.
ui_patterns.seen_in: Uber Eats 'Allergy-Friendly Restaurant Program' badge + filter shipped pattern (help.uber.com)

ui_patterns.pattern: Traffic-aware ETA via routing-matrix API, not static average
ui_patterns.detail: Compute ETA server-side using a routing/matrix API that accounts for live traffic and courier mode (walk/bike/car), validated continuously via holdout experiments — not a flat 'X–Y min' guess.
ui_patterns.seen_in: Wolt + Mapbox Matrix API case study (mapbox.com/showcase/wolt)

ui_patterns.pattern: Map re-themed via Lookup Tables per app theme
ui_patterns.detail: Use Mapbox Standard's LUT-based recoloring (roads, water, buildings, emissive glow) to produce a light map matched to HG's warm gold palette and a true dark map for dark mode, rather than shipping Mapbox's stock light/dark styles unmodified.

ui_patterns.pattern: Separate ratings for food vs. rider
ui_patterns.detail: Two distinct star ratings post-delivery (restaurant/food quality, and rider/delivery experience) rather than one blended score, so a late/rude rider doesn't corrupt a good restaurant's rating or vice versa.
ui_patterns.seen_in: DoorDash 'Rate Order: Items, Preferred Shopper' as two distinct rating surfaces (revyl.com/atlas/doordash)

ui_patterns.pattern: Every list screen ships empty/loading/error, non-negotiably
ui_patterns.detail: Saved Stores empty state, Orders history empty state, notifications empty state are each individually designed in DoorDash's shipped app rather than left as a bare blank list — matches the repo's own hard requirement.
ui_patterns.seen_in: revyl.com/atlas/doordash/ ('Saved Stores (empty state)' listed as a distinct catalogued screen)

pitfalls: Pre-selecting a high tip percentage or 'nudging' users post-checkout to raise a tip — publicly called out as a DoorDash dark pattern (phonearena.com/news/doordash-app-nudges-you-to-leave-tip_id149753); HG's tip step must default to unselected/no-tip.

Hiding service fees inside a 'tax' line to ease sticker shock at checkout — flagged explicitly as a manipulative pattern in the Uber Eats/DoorDash/Glovo teardown (luiselias.com); show every fee line separately.

Reducing allergen/dietary/halal communication to a generic free-text box — an independent audit found 80% of restaurants on DoorDash/Uber Eats have zero structured allergy-safety features (safeplatealliance.org); halal must be a structured, queryable field per restaurant/item, never a comment box.

Forcing location-permission grant with no skip option during onboarding, blocking app entry — flagged as a top usability complaint in a Deliveroo UX teardown (netguru.com/blog/deliveroo-ux-redesign-case-study).

Vague/binary 'condiments included?' style toggles standing in for real allergy or ingredient controls — DoorDash's approach was specifically criticized as 'too vague for allergy-critical users' (luiselias.com); HG's modifier sheet needs a real, always-visible instructions/ingredient field, not a buried optional toggle.

Splitting payment into a separate late-stage screen/network call that risks data loss on connection failure — flagged as a Glovo checkout weakness (luiselias.com); keep payment method + place-order in one coherent step.

Rendering a badge, icon, or color the instant a halal-check API call starts (optimistic UI) before the real certification value resolves — directly forbidden by invariant #8; use a distinct loading treatment for the certification panel specifically.

Reusing red/orange for a halal-adjacent warning (mirroring Uber Eats' orange allergy-cross-contamination banner) — directly forbidden by invariant #9; any halal ambiguity or expiry must use cool slate, and red stays reserved for unrelated, non-halal system errors only.

Using solid green for generic success states (order placed, payment succeeded) — invariant #10 reserves solid green exclusively for color.halal.*; generic success must be tint-only so it never gets confused with an active halal seal.

Burying the reorder/'Order Again' entry point only inside order history — Baymard's research shows users look for it on the homepage just as often; omitting it there reads as a broken web convention, not a minor gap.
Replaying a cached price when a user hits 'Reorder' — violates invariant #1 (server prices every order); reorder must re-price server-side since menu/price/availability may have changed.

primary_references.why: Official Deliveroo-commissioned App Store screenshot set for the rider app — useful as a visual style reference for how the brand markets/frames its rider-app screens (map, order, earnings) in a store listing.

primary_references.name: Mapbox Navigation SDK — custom theming and dark mode
primary_references.why: Since the client holds a Mapbox subscription, this is the concrete implementation path for a themed rider map: Day/Night NavigationSDK themes, automatic style switching at tunnel/time-of-day boundaries, and HD-roads styling hooks for a custom light/dark look matched to hg's palette.

steps: Sign-up (phone/email) → basic profile → vehicle type selection

Per-document upload screen: driver's licence/ID, vehicle registration & insurance (if applicable), background-check consent, profile photo — each document uploaded individually with a camera-capture UI that frames all 4 corners (Uber pattern) and gives a specific rejection reason if it fails (blurry, dark, wrong document type, missing corner)
Right-to-work / eligibility check as a distinct step, separate from vehicle documents (Deliveroo pattern) — supports passport, visa, ID card + share code variants

Selfie/liveness capture matched biometrically against the submitted ID via a third-party vendor (Deliveroo uses Onfido) — this is the moment identity fraud is caught, keep it a hard gate, not skippable
Pending-review state: explicit "under review, up to 48h" screen rather than silence (Uber SLA) — this is the single most-complained-about gap in gig onboarding UX when absent
Approval → first-trip / "accept your first delivery and earn" tutorial moment (Careem pattern) before going fully live
flows.notes: hg already treats KYC/certificates as private-bucket + presigned-URL only (repo invariant #7) — this maps cleanly onto rider onboarding documents too: never surface a public URL to a licence photo, and the pending/rejected states need their own explicit, non-optimistic UI states per the repo's empty/loading/error rule.

steps: Home screen defaults to offline state with a single unmistakable control — Wolt's "You are offline" label + "Slide to go online" slide-toggle is the clearest pattern found (deliberate friction: a slide, not a tap, to prevent accidental online status)
Going online reveals a map-first home layout (DoorDash) — map is the dominant surface, with a non-scrollable bottom sheet carrying the one actionable module for the moment (start dash / view demand)

Earnings-goal / demand surfaced contextually: DoorDash shows a headline of zone status + recommended action rather than raw noise; Wolt shows an "Expected demand today" graph and, as of 2025, live City Heat Maps of demand hotspots

Weekly-earnings pill sits in the header at all times (offline = weekly total; online = live current-session total, DoorDash's Offer Mode vs Time Mode distinction) so the rider always has a running number without opening a separate screen
Going online transitions straight into a distinct "looking for offers / waiting" state (not just a spinner) so the rider knows the app is actively working on their behalf
flows.notes: The DoorDash team's stated rule — "help Dashers decide whether it was a good time to dash without a dozen buttons, messages, and choices getting in the way" — is the single most quotable design principle for hg's rider home screen.

steps: Offer card appears as a bottom-sheet/full-card overlay over the map (not a separate screen) showing: pay amount (prominent, large type, "total may be higher" disclosure), estimated distance, item count, delivery deadline, and a small map thumbnail with pickup/dropoff pins
Countdown timer (visually a shrinking ring or bar) — DoorDash uses roughly 45 seconds; timing out counts as an automatic decline

Accept button large, high-contrast, one-tap. Decline is deliberately smaller/lower-emphasis and gated behind a 3-step flow: tap Decline → confirmation screen showing impact on acceptance rate → pick a decline reason from a list — this friction asymmetry is intentional platform behavior worth studying (and worth deliberately choosing whether to copy, given rider trust)
On accept, immediate transition to the pickup-navigation state — no intermediate screen
flows.notes: For hg, consider whether showing an acceptance-rate cost on decline fits the brand — DoorDash's drivers frequently criticize this as manipulative pressure (entrecourier.com covers driver sentiment); a cleaner, less punitive decline flow may better fit hg's 'trust' positioning while keeping the countdown and asymmetric button weight.

steps: Governing principle: the "3-Foot, 1-Second Rule" — a rider glances at the phone from ~3 feet away for ~1 second, so the screen must answer 'what's next' at a glance; everything non-essential recedes
Single-tap toggle between overview map and first-person turn-by-turn navigation, minimizing interaction while moving
Visual differentiation of pickup vs dropoff via distinct pin styles/iconography, plus side-of-street indicators and route-line previews so the rider knows which side to stop on before arriving
Camera animations and maneuver-specific icons carry the 'what turn is next' information without requiring the rider to read text
On arrival at pickup: transitions automatically (geofence-triggered) into an arrival/confirmation state rather than requiring the rider to manually declare arrival
Immediately after one leg completes, the UI pivots straight into 'what's next' — e.g., pickup confirmed → dropoff navigation begins with zero dead-end screens
Dedicated night mode: tuned separately (tested in a darkened room, then validated on real night drives) so map style and guidance UI don't blind the rider after dark
flows.notes: This is the single richest primary source for the brief's map-UX + 'single glance' requirement — quote it directly when briefing designers. Pair implementation with Mapbox Navigation SDK's Day/Night theme classes (https://docs.mapbox.com/android/navigation/examples/add-custom-theme/) which already auto-switch on time-of-day/tunnel entry, so hg's custom light/dark Mapbox style can hook into the same trigger rather than reinventing it.

steps: Geofence-triggered arrival state replaces manual 'I'm here' taps where possible
Pickup screen surfaces order-specific detail beyond the offer card: itemized contents, any pickup instructions, restaurant contact
Digital confirmation of collection (Deliveroo pattern) — an explicit 'confirm pickup' action gates the transition to dropoff navigation, so partial/wrong pickups are catchable
'No contact delivery' and similar dropoff-instruction flags are shown up front on the task card (Wolt pattern: 'Dropoff to' + 'NO CONTACT DELIVERY' badge) rather than buried in a details screen
flows.notes: Given hg's halal-verification identity, the pickup screen is a natural place to reinforce trust signaling — e.g., surfacing the restaurant's halal-certified badge state to the rider too, using the same never-red/no-optimistic-badge rules as the customer app, so riders are never shown a false certification either.

steps: At dropoff, offer OTP entry as primary path (customer-provided code) with photo capture as fallback/alternative — especially for contactless or no-answer scenarios
OTP screen kept minimal: numeric keypad, large target size, auto-advance/auto-submit on full entry — standard OTP-verification UI conventions (large digit boxes, autofill from SMS where possible)

Photo capture step includes on-device guidance (frame the doorstep/package) and immediate upload confirmation state — TLS in transit, encrypted at rest per standard delivery-workflow security guidance
Successful proof-of-delivery transitions straight to a completion/earnings-updated state — never leaves the rider on a blank or ambiguous screen
flows.notes: hg's money-model invariant (capture on acceptance, no refund-to-fail) means proof-of-delivery is not a payment gate the way it might be elsewhere — frame it purely as a dispute-evidence and trust step, and keep the UI correspondingly lightweight rather than payment-critical-feeling.

steps: Three-tab earnings IA (Uber pattern): (1) current total with a tappable, swipeable week-over-week graph, (2) Trip/Delivery History showing gross vs net per delivery, (3) Pay Summaries — weekly totals that expand into daily rows
Header-level earnings pill always visible on the home/map screen (weekly total offline, live session total online) so riders never have to leave the map to check progress
Early/instant payout option surfaced from the earnings screen (Wolt 2025 feature) — cash out immediately after a delivery rather than waiting for a weekly cycle
Demand forecasting integrated into the earnings context — 'Expected demand today' graph and heat maps — framed as a way to help riders plan when to go online, not just report the past
flows.notes: hg's ledger invariant (append-only double-entry, every order zero-residual) makes an accurate gross-vs-net-per-delivery breakdown straightforward to source directly from the ledger — the Uber IA maps onto that data model with minimal translation.

steps: Ratings tab breaks feedback into named categories (DoorDash: Communication, Followed Delivery Instructions, Order Handling, Friendliness)

Positive category feedback rendered as a green thumbs-up chip; constructive feedback (only surfaced on ≤4-star ratings) as a distinct chip — DoorDash uses red, which hg's palette rules forbid for anything read as a state judgment; use the tint/slate constructive-feedback treatment instead, never solid red
Free-text compliments surfaced separately as quoted 'Customer Compliments', decoupled from the numeric/category breakdown
Feedback is always optional from the customer side — the ratings screen must handle the empty/no-comment state gracefully, not imply a rider did something wrong when there's simply no data
flows.notes: Direct palette conflict to flag: DoorDash's red thumbs-down for critical feedback is exactly the kind of solid-red-as-judgment treatment hg's own design system forbids for halal states — for consistency, extend that same instinct here and use cool slate/neutral tint instead of red for constructive-feedback chips, keeping red-as-alarm reserved (if used at all) for true errors, not delivery quality feedback.

ui_patterns.pattern: Map-first home screen with a non-scrollable action bottom sheet
ui_patterns.detail: DoorDash's redesign made the map the dominant surface and reduced the home screen to one primary decision at a time (go online / view demand), moving everything secondary into a side menu. Directly answers the 'single glance, what do I do next' brief.

ui_patterns.pattern: Slide-to-go-online toggle (not a tap)
ui_patterns.detail: Deliberate extra friction on the state that starts earning/receiving offers, preventing accidental online status; paired with a plain-language status label ('You are offline').

ui_patterns.pattern: Offer card with shrinking countdown + asymmetric accept/decline weight
ui_patterns.detail: Pay/distance/deadline/item-count on one card with a map thumbnail; Accept large and one-tap, Decline small and gated behind a multi-step confirm+reason flow. Auto-declines on timeout (~45s).

ui_patterns.pattern: 3-Foot, 1-Second glanceability rule for active-trip UI
ui_patterns.detail: Design constraint used to strip the navigation screen to only what's needed 'right now'; single-tap toggle between overview and first-person nav; distinct pins/side-of-street indicators to disambiguate pickup vs dropoff at a glance.

ui_patterns.pattern: Communication tiering (P0/P1/P2) to protect the primary action
ui_patterns.detail: P0 = full-screen blocking takeover (account/compliance issues only), P1 = bottom-sheet overlay for decision-relevant info (incentives, zone conditions), P2 = everything else routed to a persistent Notifications Hub, never interrupting the map/offer flow.

ui_patterns.pattern: Tuned, separately-validated night mode for map + guidance UI
ui_patterns.detail: Palette tested in a darkened room in isolation, then re-validated on real night drives — a process worth copying even if hg's exact colors differ, since it directly targets rider eye-strain/safety.

ui_patterns.pattern: Three-tab earnings IA: total+graph, trip history (gross/net), weekly→daily pay summaries
ui_patterns.detail: Clean separation of 'where am I now' vs 'what happened per trip' vs 'what got paid out when' — maps cleanly onto an append-only ledger.

ui_patterns.pattern: Demand heat map + early/instant payout as earnings-screen features
ui_patterns.detail: 2025 Wolt additions: City Heat Maps show live demand hotspots to help riders decide where/when to go online; Early Payouts let riders cash out immediately after each delivery instead of waiting for a weekly cycle.

ui_patterns.pattern: Per-document capture with corner-framing guide and specific rejection reasons
ui_patterns.detail: Each onboarding document (licence, insurance, registration, background check, photo) uploaded individually via camera capture that frames all 4 corners; rejections state exactly why (blurry, dark, wrong doc type, missing corner) rather than a generic failure.

ui_patterns.pattern: Biometric selfie-to-ID liveness match as a distinct onboarding gate
ui_patterns.detail: Selfie/video captured and matched against the submitted ID via a third-party vendor (Onfido), separate step from document upload itself — a hard identity-fraud gate.

ui_patterns.pattern: Category-broken ratings with tint chips, not blanket red for criticism
ui_patterns.detail: Feedback split into named categories (Communication, Order Handling, etc.) with a positive/negative chip per category, plus a separate free-text 'Compliments' quote section; DoorDash uses green/red — hg should substitute cool slate/tint for the negative chip per its own no-red-as-judgment rule.

ui_patterns.pattern: Mapbox Navigation SDK Day/Night theme classes with automatic style switching
ui_patterns.detail: Built-in support for custom Day/Night navigation themes that switch automatically on time-of-day and tunnel entry/exit, with HD-roads styling hooks for custom road/emissive colors — the concrete implementation path for a Mapbox-based light/dark hg rider map.

pitfalls: Do not copy DoorDash's red thumbs-down / negative-feedback chip verbatim — hg's design system reserves solid red for nothing halal-state-related and generally treats red as an alarm color; use a cool-slate or tint treatment for constructive rider feedback instead, consistent with the platform's 'never red for a judgment call' instinct.

Do not let the offer-card decline flow become purely punitive. DoorDash's 3-step decline-with-acceptance-rate-impact is well-documented driver friction that generates real resentment (see entrecourier.com's driver-side account) — if hg tracks an acceptance metric at all, disclose it plainly rather than using it as a soft penalty screen sprung on decline.

Don't build a plain spinner for the 'going online / looking for offers' transition — DoorDash explicitly redesigned around this because an undifferentiated wait state reads as broken; give it its own state (e.g., 'Looking for offers near you' with the map still live).

Avoid over-cluttering the home/map screen with simultaneous banners, promos, and comms — DoorDash's whole redesign thesis was fighting exactly this; route non-critical messages to a dedicated hub (P2 tier) instead of stacking cards over the map.

Do not skip a distinct 'documents under review' state after onboarding upload — Uber's explicit up-to-48h review messaging avoids the far worse failure mode of silence, which reads as the app being broken.

Never surface a rider-facing halal-certification badge optimistically on the pickup screen if the restaurant's field is missing/expired — apply the exact same 'missing field renders no badge, never optimistic' and 'never red for expired' rules used elsewhere in hg to any halal-status surfaced to riders at pickup.

Watch the reported Deliveroo cyclist-safety complaint: routing algorithms that treat 'fastest' as synonymous with 'safest' have sent cyclists onto motorways/dual carriageways with no cycle infrastructure — if hg supports bike couriers, the Mapbox route profile needs an explicit cycling-safe mode, not just fastest-by-default.

Keep proof-of-delivery (OTP/photo) framed as evidence/trust, not as a payment gate — hg's money model captures on restaurant acceptance and has no refund-to-fail path, so a proof-of-delivery failure should not read to the rider as risking their payout, only as a dispute-record gap.

Mobbin, Behance, and some Dribbble project pages are login-gated or thin on inline descriptive text for automated fetching — treat search-result summaries and app-store/help-center pages as more reliable primary sources than scraping gated design-portfolio pages directly.

flows.flow: Halal certification verification (the seven-check instrument) — A-15
steps: Reviewer takes the next PENDING halal_certificate from a FIFO queue (mirrors A-13's take-next, SKIP LOCKED, 60-min lock) — Stripe Identity's list view equivalent: one row per certificate showing restaurant name, submitted_at, and a compact 7-dot progress indicator (checks completed/pending), no per-check detail yet.

Detail screen opens in a two-pane layout (Stripe Identity detailed-view pattern): left pane is the document image viewer (presigned URL, 5-min TTL, pinch-zoom/rotate, page navigator for multi-page scans); right pane is the transcription form — the six structured fields (certificate_number, issuing_body_id as a searchable select bound to the ACCEPTED registry only, certified_legal_name, certified_address, issued_on, expires_on, scope enum) typed directly against the document, never OCR-suggested per spec R-out-of-scope.

Below the transcription form, the seven checks render as a fixed, ordered checklist (H1-H7). H2, H5, H7 are system-computed: render them as a locked/disabled control showing the computed PASS/FAIL badge plus an info affordance (not a bare disabled toggle — wrap it so a tooltip/inline caption still explains why, since disabled elements swallow hover in most frameworks) and, on attempted override, surface the exact 409 CHECK_NOT_OVERRIDABLE message inline rather than a toast. H1, H6 are pure human judgment (radio PASS/FAIL + optional note). H3, H4 are system-suggested-admin-confirms: pre-fill a suggested PASS/FAIL with a diff view (e.g. registered legal name vs certified_legal_name side by side) and require the admin's explicit click to confirm or override; H4 override to PASS additionally hard-requires a ≥20-char note (validate client-side before enabling the confirm button, matching R5).

A sticky decision bar (Retool action-bar pattern) at the bottom: Approve is disabled until all seven checks are recorded and none is FAIL (client mirrors the 422 CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE / CHECK_FAILED server rule so the button state itself communicates readiness — a live '5 of 7 recorded' counter). Reject requires selecting one of the closed rejection_reason_code values and is enabled once ≥1 check is FAIL.

On approve/reject, show the resulting state transition inline (PENDING → APPROVED/REJECTED) and route back to the queue automatically, decrementing the queue count — avoid a modal confirm on top of an already-deliberate multi-field form; the seven-check completion IS the confirmation.
flows.notes: This is the single highest-trust screen in the whole product per CLAUDE.md ('the seal, the certification panel and the seven-check verification instrument are wrong, nothing else matters'). Every check is server-locked in the sense that H2/H5/H7 cannot be gamed by the UI — the frontend's job is to make the computed/human/hybrid distinction visually unmistakable at a glance (e.g. a small lock glyph + gray fill on computed checks vs. an editable radio group on human ones) so a reviewer never wastes time trying to override a locked check. Reference the exact H1-H7 keys from docs/spec/05-admin.md:975-985 when building fixtures.

flows.flow: Restaurant onboarding review queue — A-13 / A-14 / A-18
steps: Queue list view: FIFO by submitted_at, filterable by onboarding_state and doc completeness; 'Take next' is a single primary button above the table, not a per-row action — this enforces the no-cherry-picking rule at the UI level.

On take-next, navigate straight to the one-page review screen (spec explicitly calls for everything on one page): business identity fields, address + a Mapbox pin (client has a Mapbox subscription — render a small static/light map matched to the theme, not a full interactive map, since this is a read-only confirmation of geocoded coordinates), the four required documents each with an inline viewer + independent PENDING/APPROVED/REJECTED status and rejection_reason_code select, the halal certificate panel embedded (A-15 flow above) as a distinct sub-section, and one decision control at the bottom: Approve / Request changes / Reject.

A visible countdown or badge showing review_lock_expires_at (60-minute lock) so the reviewer knows their exclusive window; on expiry mid-review, the save action should fail fast with the 409 REVIEW_LOCK_LOST message rather than silently discarding work.

Request-changes flow: multi-select which documents are rejected with reason codes; on submit, the restaurant re-enters DOCUMENTS_SUBMITTED and submission_count increments — surface that count in the queue row for repeat-offender visibility.
flows.notes: Ground truth is docs/spec/05-admin.md:827-899 (A-13) and :911-960 (A-14). The support-agent role must NEVER see document bytes or halal check notes (A-14 R, A-15 role table) — this has to be a hard component-level gate, not a CSS hide, matching CLAUDE.md's 'hiding is cosmetic, the server check is authoritative' and its own A-42 masking rule.

flows.flow: Refund issuance with authority-cap escalation — A-33
steps: From an order detail or a case, agent opens a refund drawer: order total, remaining refundable, and a live authority meter showing the caller's remaining daily cap (e.g. 'CAD 84.00 of 150.00 remaining today') sourced from staff_refund_ledger — this is the single most important piece of context to show before the agent even picks an amount.
Scope selector: FULL / PARTIAL_ITEMS (checkbox list of line items with computed proportional tax) / PARTIAL_AMOUNT (free amount field capped client-side at remaining refundable for non-super-admins).

reason_code select (closed enum) — selecting HALAL_INTEGRITY or FOOD_SAFETY should visibly flag the refund as restaurant-liability in a small liability-split preview chip (platform/restaurant/rider cents), computed from R4's mapping, before submit.

If the computed amount exceeds the caller's cap or daily rolling total, do not block submission — per spec this must never lose the request. Instead the submit button relabels itself to 'Submit for approval' and on success shows a distinct pending-approval state (not a success toast) explaining a refund_approval_request was created and the case escalated.

Idempotency: disable the submit button immediately on click and keep it disabled through the request/response cycle (client-side belt) since the server treats a duplicate Idempotency-Key as a no-op replay, not a second refund — the UI should not rely on that safety net to permit double-clicking.
flows.notes: Ground truth: docs/spec/05-admin.md:2064-2129. The four-eyes second-approver threshold (CAD 500 for Admin, CAD 2,000 for Super Admin) is a good candidate for Stripe's dispute-evidence 'staged vs submitted' two-step pattern — draft locally, then a distinct commit action once approved.

flows.flow: Global entity search with PII masking and audited reveal — A-42
steps: A single omnibox search (Stripe/Linear Cmd+K style) across order ref, customer name/email/phone, restaurant name, restaurant id, partial address — results list shows masked values by default: phone as last-4, email as first-char+domain, address as city+partial postal code, payment instrument as brand+last4.

Every masked field renders with a small eye icon inline (not a separate settings toggle) — clicking it opens a required micro-form: case_id (searchable select, or 'no case' only for Admin+) and justification_code, before the field unmasks.

On reveal, the field unmasks in place for the session only, with a persistent visual marker (e.g. a thin colored underline) distinguishing 'this value was revealed, not natively visible' — this both reminds the agent it's sensitive and gives a re-mask affordance.

A running per-agent counter ('14 of 20 reveals this hour') visible near the search bar, going amber near the 20-reveal cap and hard-blocking with the 429 message and a plain-language cooldown timer past it.
Card PAN/CVV/full bank numbers are never given a reveal control at all — not disabled-with-tooltip, simply absent from the UI, since spec states they are not stored in retrievable form.
flows.notes: Ground truth: docs/spec/05-admin.md:2616-2655 (A-42). This is materially the same UX problem as the 'click to reveal PII, audited' pattern used in enterprise logging tools (Squiz DXP PII-HIDDEN toggle, AWS CloudWatch log masking) — search result confirms the general shape: masked-by-default, individual (never bulk) reveal, auto-re-mask on refresh/new search, and every reveal writes its own audit row. Encode the reveal rate limit and remask-on-refresh behavior as testable acceptance criteria, matching spec ACs 2/3.

flows.flow: Support case queue — pull-based assignment across SLA tiers — A-37
steps: Tier-scoped queue tabs (Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3, gated by role) each showing a 'Take next' button plus a filterable/sortable table of unassigned + own-assigned cases with columns: priority, category, SLA due countdown (color-shifts amber then to the neutral-urgent treatment as it nears breach — never red per the halal-adjacent color constraint's broader house rule of avoiding alarm-red outside genuine payment failure states), requester, age.

Case detail: three-lane message thread (PUBLIC / INTERNAL / SYSTEM) rendered as visually distinct message bubbles or left-border colors — INTERNAL must be unmistakably staff-only (e.g. a shaded background + 'Internal note — not visible to requester' label) since a same-looking bubble is the classic bug that leaks internal notes externally.

Case-link chips (order/refund/dispute/restaurant/rider) at the top of the detail pane, clickable through to the linked entity — this is what makes A-38's order-intervention and A-33's refund flows reachable in one click from a case.

State actions surfaced as a compact dropdown (Resolve / Escalate / Reassign / Merge) rather than always-visible buttons, since availability depends on role and current state — Linear's pattern of collapsing rare actions into a menu while keeping 'Take next' and 'Reply' as the two persistent primary actions.
flows.notes: Ground truth: docs/spec/05-admin.md:2347-2401. The SKIP LOCKED pull-based take-next (also used in A-13, A-15, A-23) is a recurring interaction — worth building exactly one reusable 'QueueTakeNext' component/pattern rather than three bespoke ones.

ui_patterns.pattern: Locked/computed checklist item
ui_patterns.detail: For any check the server hard-computes (H2, H5, H7 in the halal instrument), render a visually distinct 'locked' state — dimmed fill, small lock glyph, no click target on the radio itself — with the computed result still legible as a badge, and put the explanation in a wrapper element (not the disabled control) so hover/focus still shows it. Never let the UI imply the check is editable when the server will reject the override with 409.
ui_patterns.seen_in: Stripe Identity insights panel (system-computed checks shown as context, not editable) + general disabled-tooltip accessibility guidance

ui_patterns.pattern: Two-tier detail: list row summary + full detail pane
ui_patterns.detail: Every review surface (halal cert, KYC docs, disputes) should have a fast-scan list view (status chips, no images) and a separate detail view (images, full transcription, checklist) — resist the temptation to expand documents inline in the list; it kills scan speed for the queue.
ui_patterns.seen_in: Stripe Identity list view vs detailed view

ui_patterns.pattern: Status badge token contract
ui_patterns.detail: One Badge component, five semantic variants (success/error/warning/info/neutral) mapped to color tokens, Title Case text ≤2 words matching the canonical API enum value verbatim (e.g. render 'Under Review' not 'Pending'), never icon-only without a `title` attribute for screen readers. In Halal Goes, 'success' variant must resolve to the tint-only semantic-success token — solid green stays reserved to color.halal.* per the house rule, so the admin app needs its own success color distinct from the halal seal's green.

ui_patterns.pattern: URL-persisted filter/sort/pagination state
ui_patterns.detail: Every dense table's filters, sort column, and pagination cursor live in the query string so a reviewer can share or bookmark a filtered queue view (e.g. 'all P1 cases, sorted by SLA due'). Keyset/cursor pagination (not offset) for anything backed by a live queue (cases, orders, audit log) since rows are being inserted/updated concurrently by other reviewers; offset paging is acceptable only for genuinely static admin lists (e.g. issuing-body registry).
ui_patterns.seen_in: Vercel deployments filters persisted via URL; general cursor-vs-offset pagination guidance

ui_patterns.pattern: Composable headless table (filter → sort → paginate row models)
ui_patterns.detail: Build one DataTable primitive on top of a TanStack-Table-style headless row-model pipeline, then compose column sets per screen (restaurant queue columns vs rider queue columns vs audit log columns) rather than bespoke tables per screen. Bulk row-selection surfaces a floating action bar rather than per-row buttons once >1 row selected.
ui_patterns.seen_in: shadcn/ui Data Table + TanStack Table reference pattern

ui_patterns.pattern: Sticky decision/action bar on long review forms
ui_patterns.detail: For any multi-field, multi-check review (halal cert, KYC docs, refund approval), pin the terminal decision controls (Approve/Reject/Request changes) to the bottom of the viewport so the reviewer never has to scroll back up after filling the last field, and disable the primary action with a live readiness counter until preconditions are met.

ui_patterns.pattern: Authority/cap meter shown before the action, not after rejection
ui_patterns.detail: Wherever a role has a capped authority (refund caps, reveal-rate limits), show the remaining headroom as a persistent small meter near the input before the agent commits, rather than only surfacing the cap as an error after submission — turns a hard stop into a soft, informative constraint.
ui_patterns.seen_in: A-33 refund authority table; A-42 reveal rate limit; general SaaS usage-meter pattern

ui_patterns.pattern: Masked-by-default, individually-revealed, auto-remask, fully audited
ui_patterns.detail: Sensitive fields render masked; each has its own reveal control requiring justification metadata; reveals never batch; a refresh or new query re-masks everything; every reveal is its own audit row distinguishable from routine reads.
ui_patterns.seen_in: A-42 spec itself, cross-validated against enterprise log-PII masking (Squiz DXP, AWS CloudWatch) 'Logs Auditor' reveal pattern

ui_patterns.pattern: Depth via surface ladder, not shadows; single reserved accent
ui_patterns.detail: For the cleaner/sleeker direction: build 3-4 flat surface tokens (canvas → surface-1 → surface-2 → surface-3) instead of box-shadows for panel/card elevation, hairline 1px dividers on tables, and reserve exactly one accent color for primary actionable elements. In Halal Goes this reserved accent should be the brand gold — leave green completely untouched by the admin app's generic UI (buttons, links, focus rings) so it stays a halal-only signal even inside the admin console.

ui_patterns.pattern: Command palette / omnibox as the primary navigation + search entry point
ui_patterns.detail: A single Cmd/Ctrl+K-triggered global search (entities + navigation + recent cases) reduces sidebar depth needed for an ops console with this many entity types (restaurants, riders, orders, cases, disputes, staff).
ui_patterns.seen_in: Linear, Stripe Dashboard, Vercel — near-universal in this category

pitfalls: Do not let the halal seven-check UI imply H2/H5/H7 are just 'pre-filled suggestions' — they are hard server computations the admin literally cannot override (409 CHECK_NOT_OVERRIDABLE). A disabled-but-editable-looking control here is a trust bug, not a cosmetic one, given the product's single load-bearing claim is halal verification.

Never reuse a green success/checkmark for a generic admin 'approved' or 'saved' toast inside the admin app — CLAUDE.md reserves solid green exclusively to color.halal.*; the admin console needs its own tint-only semantic-success color even for non-halal approvals (KYC docs, cases, refunds).

Do not render SLA countdowns, refund-cap-exceeded states, or dispute-losing outcomes in red. Per the house rule red is reserved for reading as a religious 'haram' signal and must not leak into generic urgent/error styling elsewhere in the product; use amber/slate for urgency and a distinct (non-halal-adjacent) error hue only for hard payment/system failures.

Do not build PII reveal as a bulk 'show all' toggle on a table — spec (A-42 R) and every reference (Stripe Identity, enterprise log masking) require field-level, individually audited reveals; a table-wide unmask defeats the entire access-justification model.

Do not let the Support Agent role's UI simply CSS-hide restricted fields (document bytes, halal check notes, full PII). The API won't return them at all for that role — build components that render an explicit 'not available for your role' state when a field is absent, not components that assume the field exists and hide it client-side.

Avoid offset-based pagination ('page 1 of 340') on any queue that's actively being worked by multiple concurrent reviewers (restaurant queue, halal queue, case queue) — concurrent SKIP LOCKED takes will shift row positions under offset paging, causing reviewers to skip or double-see rows; use cursor/keyset pagination there and reserve offset-with-page-numbers for genuinely static admin lists only.

Do not surface the refund/authority cap only as a post-submit error. Spec explicitly designs the over-cap path as a graceful escalation (refund_approval_request), not a rejection — a UI that treats it as a form-validation error rather than a distinct 'submitted for approval' success state misrepresents what actually happened.

Do not visually conflate PUBLIC and INTERNAL case messages in the thread view — an internal note that looks like a customer-visible reply is the single most damaging support-tool UI bug (leaked internal commentary), and the spec explicitly forbids INTERNAL messages ever appearing in customer-facing payloads.

Avoid drop-shadow-heavy, gradient-heavy 'consumer app' chrome bleeding into the admin console — the client's HungerStation-but-cleaner direction is for the customer-facing apps; an ops console for reviewers doing hundreds of checks a day should read closer to Linear/Stripe Dashboard density than to a marketing-forward consumer UI.

icon_recommendation.why: HungerStation's bottom nav (and most modern delivery apps) uses OUTLINE icons for inactive tabs and FILLED icons for the active tab. Phosphor ships every one of its ~9,000 icons in 6 matched weights — Thin/Light/Regular/Bold/Fill/Duotone — from a single family, so inactive=Regular and active=Fill come from the SAME source with identical geometry (no compositing hacks, no second library). Duotone is ideal for the category tiles and menu-modifier illustrations. It has first-class React + React Native packages (@phosphor-icons/react, phosphor-react-native) that work across the customer/rider Expo apps and the restaurant/admin web, MIT-licensed, tree-shakeable. It is geometric and clean enough to read as 'sleek/modern' while carrying more warmth than a pure engineering set. The active-fill capability is the deciding factor: it's exactly the HS energy the client asked for, solved within one consistent family.
alternatives: Lucide — the cleanest, most tightly consistent OUTLINE set (1,500+), the safest 'sleek/minimal' default, superb lucide-react + lucide-react-native support, MIT. Downside for THIS brief: outline-only (single weight), so active-tab fills must be faked with a colored pill/background or a hand-forked filled variant. Pick Lucide if the client prefers maximum minimalism and is fine with background-fill active states.

Iconsax — very 'delivery-app modern' with Bold + Duotone variants and rounded forms that pair well with the gold; but the free tier's licensing is more restrictive than MIT, stroke consistency is looser than Phosphor/Lucide, and RN tooling is less first-class.

map_style.approach: Use @rnmapbox/maps (requires an Expo dev build — NOT Expo Go) for the customer/rider apps and mapbox-gl-js for admin web, driven by ONE Mapbox account (the client's existing subscription). Ship TWO published Mapbox Studio styles — hg-light and hg-dark — and switch by the app's color-scheme. Keep the basemap deliberately DESATURATED so the brand tint on routes and pins is the only saturated thing on screen; that restraint is what makes it read 'cleaner/sleeker' than HungerStation's default Google-style map. Verified-halal restaurant markers are the one place the halal seal green appears on the map — this is the map-pin exception already registered in tokens.json (color.halal); no other green on the map.
map_style.base_style: Fork Mapbox 'Monochrome' via the Studio Style Generator (blog.mapbox.com/custom-map-style-generator-and-monochrome-style). Seed hg-light from the warm off-white neutral.50 #FAF9F7 (start from the 'Golden' Monochrome preset, then pull saturation down so it's a warm greige, not a yellow map); seed hg-dark from the Midnight accent.950 #080F1C (near the 'Midnight' preset) so night mode matches the rider offer chrome. Alternatively fork Mapbox Standard and toggle its built-in lightPreset (day/dusk/night) via setConfigProperty for a 3D option — but Monochrome gives tighter brand control for a flat, sleek 2D map. Mute POI/road labels to neutral.500–600; let the destinations carry the color.

report.executive_summary:
Halal Goes should read as "HungerStation's energy, made cleaner." The client's reference app gets its life not from yellow alone but from a division of labor most delivery apps miss: gold is the frame (logo, active nav, "Add"/"Apply" CTAs, location pin), magenta/maroon is a dedicated PROMO register, and blue carries "free delivery" links. hg's existing gold baseline (#FFC220) already passes every contrast gate; the single missing ingredient is that promo/discount accent layer. Adding it — as an isolated namespace that never touches semantic or halal roles — is the lowest-risk way to import HungerStation's punch without recalibrating anything.

The product's one load-bearing claim is halal verification, and the research repeatedly surfaces the same structural lesson from competitors: dietary/allergen trust is almost always reduced to a generic free-text box (an independent audit found 80% of DoorDash/Uber Eats restaurants expose nothing better). hg wins by making halal a first-class, queryable field with its own filter row, its own card badge slot, and — on the restaurant page — a full certification PANEL (certifying body, expiry, seven-check summary), not a corner icon. Three invariants must be visible in every mock: a missing halal field renders NO badge (never optimistic, never a flash of green while data loads); expired/can't-vouch is cool slate, never red (red reads as a haram ruling the platform must not make); solid green is reserved to the halal seal, so generic success is tint-only.

Recommended visual direction is "Saffron Sharpened" (Direction A): keep the calibrated gold ramp and warm neutrals verbatim, add a promo family (magenta #E5157E / discount #C31B6B / HS-verified maroon #5E2D20) and a formalized link-blue (#0959B8). Icons: Phosphor (one family, matched outline+fill weights — solving the HungerStation inactive-outline/active-fill nav pattern from a single source). Maps: two published Mapbox Studio styles (hg-light forked from warm Monochrome, hg-dark from Midnight), deliberately desaturated so gold routes and pins are the only saturated thing on screen; verified-halal pins are the sole place halal green appears on the map.

Research coverage note: Customer and Rider apps are fully sourced below. The Admin ops console has strong references (Stripe Identity, Linear, shadcn Data Table, Trust & Safety queues) centered on the seven-check verification instrument. The Restaurant/merchant operator app was not covered in the source research — flagged in "apply to hg" as the top open gap to close before the client walkthrough.

report.palette_recommendation:
RECOMMENDED: Direction A — 'Saffron Sharpened' (lowest-risk blend). Keep hg's already-contrast-calibrated gold ramp and warm neutrals verbatim (they pass every gate) and add the one thing HungerStation has that hg lacks: a dedicated PROMO register plus a formalized link-blue. Primary CTA stays brand.500 #FFC220 with dark onBrand text #1F1B17 at 10.58:1 (AAA); white-on-gold stays banned (1.62:1). New promo namespace: promo.500 #E5157E (icon/large-badge only, ~4.0:1 white), promo.600 #C31B6B (discount pill, white ~5.4:1 AA), HS-verified maroon #5E2D20 (deep 'save %' pill, white ~11:1), promo.50 #FDE9F3 tint; link/info.600 #0959B8 for 'free delivery' + links. Nothing recalibrates — HungerStation's energy arrives as an accent layer. Respects every invariant: green stays halal-only, success is tint-only emerald (#067A55, no fill), halal-expired is cool slate #4E5862 (never red), promo pink/maroon are forbidden from halal and semantic roles so pink is never mistaken for a state, missing halal field still renders no badge.

Two alternatives for the walkthrough:
Direction B — 'HungerStation Bright': lift the CTA to a brighter signal-gold brand.500 #FFD400 (hue ~50, nudged AWAY from the halal-green hue; dark text ~11.8:1, actually higher contrast than today) with a hotter promo shelf. Choose if the client wants the app visibly louder/younger. Deliberately avoids HS's true #FBEF00 acid lemon, which leans chartreuse toward green and is unusable next to a green seal.

Direction C — 'Gold + Maroon Duotone' (premium/editorial): gold for action, HS maroon #5E2D20 as warm secondary chrome/AppBar (white labels ~11:1) over old-HG cream #FFFAEA canvas — a warm 'trusted marketplace' feel that quietly honors the old brand's cream while abandoning its now-forbidden forest green. Maroon is used ONLY as chrome, never as a state, so danger stays true red #D92D20 (semantic only, never halal). Choose if the brand should feel less 'delivery-app loud.'

Note for the client: the OLD Halal Goes was forest-green-forward (#1B3B31 + cream). That green now COLLIDES with invariant #10 — reviving it as chrome would break the halal signal. The pivot to gold isn't just aesthetic; it freed green to mean 'halal-verified' exclusively. Reuse the old logo only if re-colored to gold; do not reintroduce #1B3B31 or the old orange #FD5000.
report.icon_and_map:
ICONS — Phosphor Icons. HungerStation (and most modern delivery apps) uses outline icons for inactive tabs and FILLED icons for the active tab. Phosphor ships all ~9,000 icons in 6 matched weights (Thin/Light/Regular/Bold/Fill/Duotone) from ONE family, so inactive=Regular and active=Fill share identical geometry — no second library, no compositing hacks. Duotone suits the category tiles and menu-modifier illustrations. First-class React + React Native packages (@phosphor-icons/react, phosphor-react-native) cover both Expo apps and both web consoles; MIT, tree-shakeable. The active-fill capability is the deciding factor — it's exactly the HS nav energy, solved in one consistent family. Alternatives: Lucide (cleanest outline-only set — pick if the client wants maximum minimalism and accepts background-fill active states); Iconsax (very delivery-app-modern but looser stroke consistency and non-MIT free tier); SF Symbols EXCLUDED (Apple-only, breaks cross-platform parity).

MAPS — Mapbox on the client's existing single account. Use @rnmapbox/maps for the Expo apps (requires an Expo DEV BUILD, not Expo Go) and mapbox-gl-js for admin web. Ship TWO published Mapbox Studio styles, hg-light and hg-dark, switched by color-scheme. Fork Mapbox 'Monochrome' via the Studio Style Generator: seed hg-light from warm neutral #FAF9F7 (start from the 'Golden' preset, pull saturation down to a warm greige), seed hg-dark from Midnight #080F1C so night matches the rider offer chrome. Keep the basemap deliberately DESATURATED and mute POI/road labels to neutral 500-600 — that restraint is what reads 'cleaner than HungerStation.' Route line = gold #FFC220 core with a #DFA400 casing on light (step up to #FFDB69 on dark for ≥3:1). Customer location + delivery pins = gold; rider live marker = the operational Midnight #24406F (Dir A/B) or maroon #5E2D20 (Dir C), kept distinct from the gold route; destination pin = neutral #1F1B17 teardrop. Verified-halal restaurant markers are the ONE place halal seal green (#04482A light / #0F7A46 dark, brass ring) appears on the map — the registered map-pin exception; non-verified restaurants get a neutral #4A443B pin with NO green (invariant #8). Never red for any halal or unavailable-restaurant map state — use neutral/slate. For ETA, use the Mapbox Matrix API (traffic- and courier-mode-aware, validated by Wolt's switchback experiments) plus Static Maps for lightweight tracking images — not a flat average. On the rider side, hook Mapbox Navigation SDK's built-in Day/Night theme classes (auto-switch on time-of-day/tunnel) into the same custom styles.
apply_to_hg: 1. Close the Restaurant/merchant operator research gap BEFORE the client walkthrough — it is the one app with zero source coverage. Mine FoodMagic (dribbble 22162296), Shopify Polaris (table/empty-state/voice), and Uber Base; storyboard the order-accept queue (it is the authorise→capture trigger, invariant #5) and a non-green availability toggle. This is the top open blocker.

2. Add the promo/link accent layer to tokens.json now (Direction A): promo.500 #E5157E, promo.600 #C31B6B, promo.maroon #5E2D20, promo.50 #FDE9F3, link/info.600 #0959B8. Wire lint so promo.* is forbidden from halal.* and from semantic success/danger roles — this is what safely imports HungerStation's energy without recalibration.

3. Build the halal certification PANEL component (restaurant page) with its OWN loading skeleton distinct from generic content skeletons, plus the card-level badge SLOT that renders nothing on null/loading. Prove invariant #8 (no optimistic badge, no green flash) and invariant #9 (expired = slate #4E5862) in a real mock, both themes. Highest-trust surface in the product.

4. Make 'Halal Certified' a first-class filter section pinned at the top of the filter bottom sheet (not alphabetized among vegan/gluten-free) and a distinct home-screen category tile — signals platform guarantee vs per-user preference.

5. Ship the two Mapbox Studio styles (hg-light from warm Monochrome, hg-dark from Midnight), desaturated, with the gold route + halal-green verified pin exception. Confirm the Expo apps move to a DEV BUILD (rnmapbox needs it — not Expo Go); note this against the known Expo Go constraint of the (since removed) native component gallery. Adopt Matrix API for ETA, not a static average.
6. Adopt Phosphor across all four apps; standardize the nav pattern as Regular (inactive) + Fill (active) from the single family, and the delivery-time shield glyph on restaurant cards.

7. Bake the anti-dark-pattern stances into the design spec as hard rules: tip defaults UNSELECTED with 'No tip' at equal weight (counter DoorDash); fee breakdown EXPANDED by default (no fees hidden in tax); payment + place-order in ONE step (no Glovo-style late round-trip); reorder RE-PRICES server-side (invariant #1); 'Order Again' rail in the homepage first viewport (Baymard).

8. Rider: implement P0/P1/P2 comms tiering and a differentiated 'looking for offers' state (not a spinner) around a map-first home; use the 3-foot/1-second rule as the active-trip design constraint; keep the offer countdown but make the decline flow non-punitive (disclose any acceptance metric plainly). Enforce the KYC document flow as private-bucket + presigned (invariant #7) with an explicit 'under review up to 48h' state.

9. Enforce hg's palette discipline everywhere feedback/ratings appear: separate food-vs-rider ratings (customer) and category-broken ratings with TINT/slate chips, never DoorDash's solid-red thumbs-down. Extend 'never red for a judgment call' from halal state to all quality feedback.

10. Admin seven-check instrument (A-15): build the two-pane list+detail with the H1-H7 typology explicit in the UI — computed checks (H2/H5/H7) as locked badges surfacing 409 inline, human checks (H1/H6), and confirm-with-diff checks (H3/H4, H4→PASS gated on a ≥20-char note). Live 'N of 7 recorded' counter drives the Approve button state. Give the admin a single non-halal-green accent (Linear discipline).

11. Every screen in every app ships empty/loading/error — repo-level hard requirement; specifically design Saved Stores empty, Orders empty, Notifications empty, all admin queues empty, and the halal 'not yet loaded' vs 'no badge' distinction.
